name: Red on the Map: Britain and Its Empire
description: How traders, sailors, soldiers and reformers made a quarter of the world British, and how the empire was taken apart again, from Virginia to Hong Kong.

checkpoints.name: Merchants and colonies
checkpoints.note: Under Elizabeth I the East India Company is founded, and under James I the Virginia Company plants colonies. The Royal African Company feeds the Atlantic slave trade, and victory at Plassey and Cook's voyage widen Britain's reach.

checkpoints.name: War and abolition
checkpoints.note: The loss of the American colonies in the Revolutionary War turns Britain toward Asia. Nelson's win at Trafalgar secures the seas, Company rule spreads in India, and the Slavery Abolition Act ends slavery in most of the empire.

checkpoints.name: The Victorian peak
checkpoints.note: Under Queen Victoria the empire reaches its height. The Opium War gives Britain Hong Kong, the Great Exhibition shows off its industry, the 1857 rebellion leads to the Raj, and Rhodes and the Scramble for Africa bring new wars with the Zulu and Boers.

checkpoints.name: Strain and awakening
checkpoints.note: The empire is stretched by world wars while Indian nationalism grows. Gandhi's Salt March shows the power of mass protest, and the British Empire begins to lose its hold on its richest colony.

checkpoints.name: The flags come down
checkpoints.note: India and Pakistan are born in the Partition of India, the Suez crisis exposes Britain's weakness, and the Mau Mau rebellion in Kenya shakes colonial rule. Nkrumah's Ghana is the first British colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence, and Hong Kong returns to China in 1997.
